---
title: "Example: volcano plot"
description: >
  A small analysis app with hosted inputs, value boxes and a Shiny module,
  with a Python server and a React client.
---

`examples/volcano-plot` is a small analysis app with the usual bslib shape:
controls in a sidebar, a row of value boxes, and a plot in a card. It was
ported from a plain bslib app, and the server kept its shape. Only the layout
moved to React.

![The volcano plot app: five controls in a sidebar, three value boxes
counting up, down and not significant genes, and a volcano plot in a
card.](https://www.samuelbharti.com/bslibreact/assets/volcano-py.png)

## Run it

The built client is committed, so the app runs without Node:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/samuelbharti/bslibreact.git
pip install bslibreact shinyreact pandas matplotlib brand_yml
shiny run bslibreact/examples/volcano-plot/app.py
```

## The page

`src/App.tsx` lays out the whole page. Each component stands for one call:
`PageSidebar` for `ui.page_sidebar()`, `LayoutColumns` for
`ui.layout_columns()`, `ValueBox` for `ui.value_box()`, `Card` for
`ui.card()`.

```tsx
<PageSidebar title="Volcano plot" sidebarWidth={290} sidebar={<Sidebar />}>
  <LayoutColumns colWidths={[4, 4, 4]} fill={false}>
    <ValueBox title="Up" theme="warning">
      <TextOutput id="n_up" className="value-box-value" />
    </ValueBox>
    <ValueBox title="Down" theme="primary">
      <TextOutput id="n_down" className="value-box-value" />
    </ValueBox>
    <ValueBox title="Not significant" theme="secondary">
      <TextOutput id="n_ns" className="value-box-value" />
    </ValueBox>
  </LayoutColumns>
  <Card fullScreen>
    <CardHeader>Differential expression: synthetic dataset</CardHeader>
    <CardBody>
      <Module namespace="volcano">
        <PlotOutput id="plot" height="560px" click="click" />
      </Module>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</PageSidebar>
```

## Five hosted inputs

The sidebar holds two threshold sliders, a radio group, a checkbox and a
label count slider. The server renders each one with `host_input()`, so
they are Shiny's own widgets:

```python
host_input(
    output,
    "lfc",
    lambda: ui.input_slider("lfc", "|log2 fold change| threshold", 0, 5, 1, step=0.1),
)
host_input(
    output,
    "pcol",
    lambda: ui.input_radio_buttons(
        "pcol", "Significance metric", {"padj": "Adjusted p", "pvalue": "Raw p"}
    ),
)
host_input(
    output, "dolabel", lambda: ui.input_checkbox("dolabel", "Label top genes", True)
)
```

The client mounts each one by its id plus `_ui`, with the component that
matches the widget:

```tsx
function Sidebar() {
  return (
    <>
      <SliderInput id="lfc_ui" />
      <SliderInput id="p_ui" />
      <RadioButtons id="pcol_ui" />
      <CheckboxInput id="dolabel_ui" />
      <SliderInput id="topn_ui" />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Waiting for the inputs

A hosted input has no value until the client has mounted it. Reading it
before then stops the calculation silently, so the plot and the counts stay
blank until every input has arrived. The server needs no extra code for
this:

```python
vdata = volcano_server(
    "volcano",
    lfc_threshold=lambda: input.lfc(),
    p_threshold=lambda: input.p(),
    p_col=lambda: input.pcol(),
    label_top_n=lambda: input.topn() if input.dolabel() else 0,
)
```

## A plot inside a Shiny module

The plot is rendered by a real module, declared with `@module.server` and
called as `volcano_server("volcano", ...)`, so its output id on the page is
`volcano-plot`. On the client, `<Module namespace="volcano">` adds the same
prefix to every id inside it, so `<PlotOutput id="plot" />` displays
`volcano-plot`.

## Value boxes that read text

The three counts are plain `@render.text` outputs:

```python
@reactive.calc
def counts():
    return volcano_status_counts(vdata())

@render.text
def n_up():
    return str(counts()["Up"])
```

Each one shows through a `<TextOutput>` inside a `<ValueBox>`. The value box
itself is React markup and needs nothing from the server.
